treatment.name: Dental Implants
treatment.overview: Dental implants are permanent, natural-looking replacements for missing teeth. A titanium post fuses with your jawbone and supports a custom crown for stable chewing and confident smiling.

types.name: Single-Tooth Implant
description: Replaces one missing tooth with a titanium post and crown.
Preserves adjacent teeth—no need to file them.

types.name: Multiple Implants / Bridge on Implants
description: Replaces several missing teeth with fewer implant posts.
Distributes bite forces efficiently for durability.

types.name: Full-Arch (All-on-4 / All-on-6)
description: Rehabilitates an entire jaw using 4–6 implants.
Fixed teeth solution for denture wearers.

cost.note: Final cost depends on number of implants, bone condition, and crown material after evaluation.

before: Consultation with X-ray/CBCT and treatment planning.
Assessment of bone and gums; graft/sinus lift if required.
Discussion of timelines and crown options.
during: Impressions/scans for custom abutment and crown.
after: Final crown/bridge delivery and bite adjustments.
Strict oral hygiene around implant and regular reviews.
Avoid smoking/excessive force to enhance longevity.

avoid: Very hard foods on the implant during early healing
prefer: Soft foods for 48–72 hours after surgery
foodGuidelines.tip: Rinse gently with prescribed mouthwash/saline; do not disturb the surgical site.

pros: No surgical procedure or recovery time
cons: Progressive bone loss in the missing tooth area
Shifting of adjacent teeth and bite changes
Future replacements may become more complex/costly
prosConsOfSkipping.summary: Implants preserve bone, restore function and aesthetics, and help protect overall oral health.

faq.a: With good hygiene and regular check-ups, implants can last decades—often a lifetime.
It’s done under local anesthesia; most patients report only mild post-op soreness.

faq.q: When will I get the crown?
faq.a: After osseointegration (typically 3–6 months) or sooner in select immediate-loading cases.
